summary: The bill amends the tax code to permanently codify and extend through 2026 the rules allowing individuals to deduct qualified net disaster losses from major disasters (with a $100 floor and above the 10% AGI threshold) even if they do not itemize, and to exclude from gross income compensation received for losses from federally declared forest or range fires.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the tax code to provide deductions and income exclusions for disaster-related losses. It does not authorize or modify any direct government expenditures or appropriations, so it has no bearing on government spending levels.

The legislation codifies and extends favorable tax treatment under IRC section 165 for personal casualty losses from major disasters (including lowering the floor and allowing above-the-line deductions) and adds a new exclusion under section 139M for qualified wildfire relief payments. These changes reduce taxable income for affected individuals, constituting targeted tax relief.
No provisions address healthcare coverage, insurance mandates, public programs, or market-based reforms.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense budgets or policy.
While the bill references wildfire and disaster losses, it only provides tax relief and does not create, expand, or limit any environmental regulations or protections.
The bill provides tax relief rather than expanding or contracting entitlement programs such as welfare or food assistance.
No provisions address schools, school choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.

By extending tax relief that reduces federal revenue, the bill could marginally increase deficits, but it does not contain any explicit provisions or directives regarding debt reduction or deficit spending priorities.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil rights enforcement.
